goodish.oewn-01128140-s.label: neutral
goodish.oewn-01128140-s.tone: Grudging - good, but only moderately, and the word admits it.

acceptable.oewn-01128566-s.label: neutral
acceptable.oewn-01128566-s.tone: Clears the bar and no more; in speech it often signals mild disappointment.

satisfactory.oewn-01128566-s.label: neutral
satisfactory.oewn-01128566-s.tone: Meets the requirement - the language of reports and inspections, not of praise.

decent.oewn-01128566-s.label: positive
decent.oewn-01128566-s.tone: Warm but modest - better than expected without being remarkable.

good.oewn-01126910-a.label: positive
good.oewn-01126910-a.tone: The plain word of approval - broad, safe, and unemphatic.
examples: a good meal and good company

solid.oewn-01128873-s.label: positive
solid.oewn-01128873-s.tone: Praises dependability rather than brilliance - built to last.

great.oewn-01127641-s.label: positive
great.oewn-01127641-s.tone: Everyday enthusiasm - the common word for real approval.
examples: That was a great film.

excellent.oewn-02351216-s.label: positive
excellent.oewn-02351216-s.tone: Unqualified praise - at the top of its class.

superb.oewn-01129021-s.label: positive
superb.oewn-01129021-s.tone: Surpassing praise, with a note of polish and craft.
examples: a superb performance from the whole cast

dandy.oewn-01127641-s.label: positive
dandy.oewn-01127641-s.tone: Old-fashioned cheer - now often used ironically.

groovy.oewn-01127641-s.label: positive
groovy.oewn-01127641-s.tone: Period slang; using it today reads as deliberately retro.

mediocre.oewn-01132084-s.label: negative
mediocre.oewn-01132084-s.tone: Damns by middling - not bad enough to condemn, not good enough to praise.
mediocre.oewn-01132084-s.explanation: The insult is the absence of merit, not the presence of fault.
examples: a mediocre film that nobody remembers

bad.oewn-01129296-a.label: negative
bad.oewn-01129296-a.tone: The plain word of disapproval - broad and unemphatic.
examples: bad weather
a bad decision

lousy.oewn-01131613-s.label: negative
lousy.oewn-01131613-s.tone: Casual disgust - everyday, forceful, and slightly coarse.

rotten.oewn-01131613-s.label: negative
rotten.oewn-01131613-s.tone: Thoroughly bad, with a hint of moral distaste.

crappy.oewn-01131613-s.label: negative
crappy.oewn-01131613-s.tone: Crude dismissal - fine among friends, out of place in writing.

awful.oewn-01130122-s.label: negative
awful.oewn-01130122-s.tone: Strong condemnation, common enough to have lost some of its force.
examples: an awful mistake

dreadful.oewn-01130122-s.label: negative
dreadful.oewn-01130122-s.tone: Emphatic disapproval with a formal, slightly literary edge.

terrible.oewn-01130122-s.label: negative
terrible.oewn-01130122-s.tone: Blunt and total - among the strongest everyday condemnations.

atrocious.oewn-01130122-s.label: negative
atrocious.oewn-01130122-s.tone: Severe and formal - originally of cruelty, now also of quality.
atrocious.oewn-01130122-s.explanation: Carries a residue of moral horror even when used of a meal.
examples: atrocious handwriting
atrocious treatment of prisoners

abominable.oewn-01130122-s.label: negative
abominable.oewn-01130122-s.tone: Moral revulsion - condemns rather than criticises.

deplorable.oewn-01130672-s.label: negative
deplorable.oewn-01130672-s.tone: Formal censure, expecting the reader to share the judgement.

naughty.oewn-01132237-s.label: negative
naughty.oewn-01132237-s.tone: Affectionate scolding - too light to carry a real fault.

slow.oewn-00442596-s.label: negative
slow.oewn-00442596-s.tone: The softened word - avoids naming a deficit outright.

dense.oewn-00442596-s.label: negative
dense.oewn-00442596-s.tone: Mild and often jokey - failing to grasp what is plain.

dim.oewn-00442596-s.label: negative
dim.oewn-00442596-s.tone: Gently disparaging, common in British use.

obtuse.oewn-00442596-s.label: negative
obtuse.oewn-00442596-s.tone: Formal reproach - slow to understand, and perhaps unwilling to.

stupid.oewn-00441328-a.label: negative
stupid.oewn-00441328-a.tone: The blunt, wounding word - a flat verdict on someone's mind.
stupid.oewn-00441328-a.explanation: Direct enough that most speakers reach for a softer term when they mean it kindly.
examples: It was a stupid thing to say.

dumb.oewn-00442596-s.label: negative
dumb.oewn-00442596-s.tone: Harsh and casual; also an older, now offensive word for mute.
dumb.oewn-00442596-s.explanation: Avoid of people - it insults rather than describes.

foolish.oewn-00441663-s.label: negative
foolish.oewn-00441663-s.tone: Faults the judgement rather than the intelligence - a wise person can act foolishly.
examples: a foolish risk to take with someone else's money

asinine.oewn-00442050-s.label: negative
asinine.oewn-00442050-s.tone: Withering - stupidity so complete it deserves contempt.

inane.oewn-00442050-s.label: negative
inane.oewn-00442050-s.tone: Empty of sense - condemns the content, not the person.

gormless.oewn-00443171-s.label: negative
gormless.oewn-00443171-s.tone: British informal - vacant and hopeless with it.

bright.oewn-01338411-s.label: positive
bright.oewn-01338411-s.tone: Warm and everyday: quickness to learn, praised without ceremony.
examples: a bright student who asks good questions

smart.oewn-01338411-s.label: positive
smart.oewn-01338411-s.tone: Common approval of quickness; in some uses it edges toward cunning.

clever.oewn-01337910-s.label: positive
clever.oewn-01337910-s.tone: Praises ingenuity - though 'too clever' turns it into a fault.
clever.oewn-01337910-s.explanation: Approving of resourcefulness, with a faint warning attached.
examples: a clever solution nobody else saw

apt.oewn-01337910-s.label: positive
apt.oewn-01337910-s.tone: Quick to learn - formal and slightly old-fashioned.

intelligent.oewn-01337350-a.label: positive
intelligent.oewn-01337350-a.tone: The neutral, respectable word - approving without flourish.
examples: an intelligent reading of a difficult text

quick.oewn-01338856-s.label: positive
quick.oewn-01338856-s.tone: Praises speed of understanding rather than depth.

brilliant.oewn-01338108-s.label: positive
brilliant.oewn-01338108-s.tone: Exceptional intelligence - the strongest ordinary compliment.
brilliant.oewn-01338108-s.explanation: Marks someone out from the merely clever.
examples: a brilliant mathematician

trenchant.oewn-01339324-s.label: positive
trenchant.oewn-01339324-s.tone: Sharp and penetrating - praise for incisive thought.

pretty.oewn-00221674-s.label: positive
pretty.oewn-00221674-s.tone: Pleasing but slight - delicate rather than striking, and faintly diminishing.
pretty.oewn-00221674-s.explanation: Approving, though it implies charm rather than power.
examples: a pretty little garden

bonny.oewn-00220032-s.label: positive
bonny.oewn-00220032-s.tone: Scottish and northern English warmth - healthy and pleasing.

handsome.oewn-00220542-s.label: positive
handsome.oewn-00220542-s.tone: Praises strong, well-proportioned looks; dignity rather than prettiness.

good-looking.oewn-00220542-s.label: positive
good-looking.oewn-00220542-s.tone: Plain, unfussy approval - the everyday compliment.

lovely.oewn-00221401-s.label: positive
lovely.oewn-00221401-s.tone: Warm and affectionate - beauty that moves the feelings, not just the eye.

beautiful.oewn-00219320-a.label: positive
beautiful.oewn-00219320-a.tone: The full word - unreserved and applicable to anything from a face to an argument.
examples: a beautiful morning
a beautiful proof

exquisite.oewn-00220429-s.label: positive
exquisite.oewn-00220429-s.tone: Beauty of fine detail - praise for delicacy and craft.

gorgeous.oewn-00221297-s.label: positive
gorgeous.oewn-00221297-s.tone: Dazzling and enthusiastic - beauty that stops you.

ravishing.oewn-00222094-s.label: positive
ravishing.oewn-00222094-s.tone: Overwhelming beauty - lush and a little theatrical.

dishy.oewn-00220265-s.label: positive
dishy.oewn-00220265-s.tone: British slang for sexually attractive - casual and now somewhat dated.

unlovely.oewn-00224041-s.label: negative
unlovely.oewn-00224041-s.tone: Understated - withholds beauty rather than asserting ugliness.
unlovely.oewn-00224041-s.explanation: The gentlest way to say it.

plain.oewn-00170694-s.label: negative
plain.oewn-00170694-s.tone: Polite avoidance - unremarkable rather than unattractive.

unsightly.oewn-00224135-s.label: negative
unsightly.oewn-00224135-s.tone: Offends the eye - used more comfortably of things than of people.

ugly.oewn-00222548-a.label: negative
ugly.oewn-00222548-a.tone: The blunt word, and a wounding one of a person.
ugly.oewn-00222548-a.explanation: Passes flat judgement on appearance; most speakers soften it when they can.
examples: an ugly concrete tower
There is no kind way to call someone ugly.

grotesque.oewn-00223219-s.label: negative
grotesque.oewn-00223219-s.tone: Distorted to the point of unsettling - beyond plain ugliness.

monstrous.oewn-00223219-s.label: negative
monstrous.oewn-00223219-s.tone: Ugliness that frightens; also used of moral wrong.

hideous.oewn-00223526-s.label: negative
hideous.oewn-00223526-s.tone: Extreme and repellent - among the harshest words available.
examples: a hideous scar left by the fire

repulsive.oewn-00223526-s.label: negative
repulsive.oewn-00223526-s.tone: Ugliness that actively drives people away.

fugly.oewn-00223145-s.label: negative
fugly.oewn-00223145-s.tone: Crude insult built from an obscenity - offensive in any setting.

hard_up.oewn-02030912-s.label: negative
hard_up.oewn-02030912-s.tone: Temporary and undramatic - short of money this month, not poor in life.

broke.oewn-02030538-s.label: negative
broke.oewn-02030538-s.tone: Casual and often self-applied - out of money right now.
examples: I'm broke until payday.

poor.oewn-02030204-a.label: negative
poor.oewn-02030204-a.tone: The plain word for a lasting condition - factual, but heavy enough that officials avoid it.
examples: a poor family in a rich country

impecunious.oewn-02030912-s.label: negative
impecunious.oewn-02030912-s.tone: Genteel and bookish - poverty at a polite distance.

penniless.oewn-02030912-s.label: negative
penniless.oewn-02030912-s.tone: Absolute and vivid - not a coin left.

needy.oewn-02030681-s.label: negative
needy.oewn-02030681-s.tone: Frames poverty as requiring help; of a person's temperament it means something else entirely.

impoverished.oewn-02030681-s.label: negative
impoverished.oewn-02030681-s.tone: Made poor - the word implies something was taken away.
impoverished.oewn-02030681-s.explanation: Points at a cause rather than blaming the poor.

indigent.oewn-02030681-s.label: negative
indigent.oewn-02030681-s.tone: The legal and administrative term for qualifying poverty.

destitute.oewn-02030681-s.label: negative
destitute.oewn-02030681-s.tone: Total and grave - without even the means to live.
examples: The fire left them destitute.

poverty-stricken.oewn-02030681-s.label: negative
poverty-stricken.oewn-02030681-s.tone: Poverty as an affliction that has struck, not a state chosen.

comfortable.oewn-02029807-s.label: positive
comfortable.oewn-02029807-s.tone: The modest way to say it - enough money, and no wish to discuss it.

well-off.oewn-02029807-s.label: positive
well-off.oewn-02029807-s.tone: Plainly better off than most, without ostentation.

prosperous.oewn-02029807-s.label: positive
prosperous.oewn-02029807-s.tone: Wealth read as the reward of success - approving.

affluent.oewn-02029380-s.label: positive
affluent.oewn-02029380-s.tone: The neutral term of economists and estate agents.

wealthy.oewn-02029380-s.label: positive
wealthy.oewn-02029380-s.tone: Substantial and settled money - more dignified than 'rich'.

rich.oewn-02029118-a.label: positive
rich.oewn-02029118-a.tone: The plain word - direct, and sometimes faintly accusing depending on who says it.
examples: rich enough never to check a price

moneyed.oewn-02029380-s.label: neutral
moneyed.oewn-02029380-s.tone: States wealth. Whether wealth is a credit is left to the reader.

flush.oewn-02029380-s.label: positive
flush.oewn-02029380-s.tone: Temporarily well supplied - this week, not for life.

loaded.oewn-02029380-s.label: positive
loaded.oewn-02029380-s.tone: Blunt and slightly envious - conspicuously rich.
examples: Her family is absolutely loaded.

well-heeled.oewn-02029807-s.label: positive
well-heeled.oewn-02029807-s.tone: Comfortably moneyed, with a wry edge.

game.oewn-00264860-s.label: positive
game.oewn-00264860-s.tone: Willing to try - courage as good sportsmanship rather than heroism.

gritty.oewn-00264860-s.label: positive
gritty.oewn-00264860-s.tone: Courage as endurance - staying in when it hurts.

spunky.oewn-00264860-s.label: positive
spunky.oewn-00264860-s.tone: Affectionate praise for spirit, often of someone small taking on something large.

brave.oewn-00263658-a.label: positive
brave.oewn-00263658-a.tone: The plain, universal praise - facing what frightens you.
examples: a brave decision to speak up

courageous.oewn-00263658-a.label: positive
courageous.oewn-00263658-a.tone: Weightier than 'brave' - implies moral choice, not just nerve.

valiant.oewn-00265436-s.label: positive
valiant.oewn-00265436-s.tone: Heroic register, at home in battle and legend.

stouthearted.oewn-00265128-s.label: positive
stouthearted.oewn-00265128-s.tone: Steadfast courage - praise with a Victorian ring.

undaunted.oewn-00265325-s.label: positive
undaunted.oewn-00265325-s.tone: Courage defined by what failed to stop it.

heroic.oewn-00264329-s.label: positive
heroic.oewn-00264329-s.tone: Courage beyond what could be asked of anyone.

timid.oewn-00266855-s.label: negative
timid.oewn-00266855-s.tone: Gentle - shyness rather than failure of nerve, and rarely an accusation.

fainthearted.oewn-00266855-s.label: negative
fainthearted.oewn-00266855-s.tone: Lacking boldness - mild, and often used of a task rather than a person.

fearful.oewn-00265642-a.label: negative
fearful.oewn-00265642-a.tone: Names the fear without judging the person for it.

cowardly.oewn-00265642-a.label: negative
cowardly.oewn-00265642-a.tone: The plain accusation - fear that led to failing others.
cowardly.oewn-00265642-a.explanation: Condemns the choice, not the feeling.
examples: a cowardly refusal to take responsibility

chicken.oewn-00266180-s.label: negative
chicken.oewn-00266180-s.tone: Playground taunt - mocking rather than grave.

lily-livered.oewn-00266180-s.label: negative
lily-livered.oewn-00266180-s.tone: Old-fashioned scorn from a theory that pale organs meant no courage.

craven.oewn-00266362-s.label: negative
craven.oewn-00266362-s.tone: Abject cowardice - formal and thoroughly contemptuous.

dastardly.oewn-00266631-s.label: negative
dastardly.oewn-00266631-s.tone: Cowardice joined to malice; now often played for comedy.

pusillanimous.oewn-00267286-s.label: negative
pusillanimous.oewn-00267286-s.tone: Bookish contempt - small-spirited in the face of difficulty.
